about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Achari Baingan Pickled Eggplant
recipes.summary: Eggplant fried until golden then tossed in a mustard, chilli and vinegar pickle masala, a tangy side for dal and rice.
steps: Heat half the oil in a wide frying pan and fry the eggplant in two batches for 6 minutes each, until golden and soft, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the mustard seeds, and cook for 30 seconds until they pop.
Stir in the garlic, turmeric, chilli and cumin for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the eggplant with the vinegar, sugar and salt and toss for 2 minutes, until glossy.
Cool and spoon into a clean jar.
notes: Keeps 1 week in the fridge in a clean, sterilised jar with the oil sealing the top; use a clean spoon each time and discard if it smells off or shows mould.

recipes.title: Indian Nimbu Achar Lime Pickle
recipes.summary: Lime wedges softened in salt and spices, a sharp, salty pickle to serve in small amounts with curries.
steps: Toss the limes with the salt and turmeric in a clean bowl and pack into a sterilised jar.
Press down, cover and leave on a sunny bench for 3 days, shaking each day, until the peel softens and the juice rises.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the mustard seeds for 30 seconds until they pop.
Stir in the chilli, cumin and sugar for 20 seconds, then pour over the limes and mix well.
Seal and rest 1 week before eating, then store in the fridge.
notes: Fermenting and resting time is not included in prep. Use a sterilised jar, keep the limes under the brine and discard the jar if mould forms or it smells unpleasant. Keeps 2 months in the fridge. Serve in small amounts because it is very salty.

recipes.title: Gajar Achar Carrot and Chilli Pickle
recipes.summary: A crunchy fridge pickle of carrot and green chilli in mustard oil style brine, ready in two days.

items: 2 tbsp brown mustard seeds, lightly crushed

steps: Heat the water, salt, vinegar and sugar until the salt dissolves, then cool completely.
Pack the carrot and chilli into a sterilised jar.
Mix the mustard seeds, turmeric and oil and stir through the carrot.
Pour in the cooled brine until the vegetables are covered.
Seal and leave at room temperature for 2 days, then refrigerate.
notes: Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge. Keep the vegetables submerged under the brine, use a clean spoon, and discard if cloudy with a bad smell, slime or mould.

recipes.title: Kerala Style Green Mango Pickle
recipes.summary: Firm green mango in a fiery chilli and mustard oil, the classic salty pickle that lifts plain rice and yoghurt.

items: 3 green mangoes, cut in 2cm pieces with skin

steps: Toss the mango with the salt and turmeric, cover and stand for 12 hours, then drain the liquid.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the mustard seeds for 30 seconds until they pop.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the chilli and cumin for 20 seconds.
Cool the oil completely, then mix with the mango.
Pack into a sterilised jar with the oil covering the top.
notes: Standing time is not included in prep. Cool the oil fully before mixing so the mango stays crisp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge; use a dry spoon, keep the mango under the oil and discard if mould appears.

recipes.title: Coconut Chutney South Indian Style
recipes.summary: Fresh coconut ground with green chilli, ginger and roasted chickpeas, served with dosa and idli.

items: 200g desiccated coconut, soaked in warm water and drained

steps: Blend the coconut, chickpeas, green chilli, ginger, salt and water to a coarse paste, adding a little more water if needed.
Spoon the chutney into a serving bowl and smooth the top.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the mustard seeds and dried chilli for 30 seconds, until the seeds pop.
Pour the hot tempering over the chutney.
Serve within a few hours.
notes: Best the day it is made; keeps 2 days in the fridge in a covered container.

recipes.title: Tomato Kuthu Chutney Spicy Roast Tomato Chutney
recipes.summary: Tomatoes and chilli cooked down until jammy and ground with garlic, a quick chutney for flatbread and eggs.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the chilli and mustard seeds for 30 seconds, until the seeds pop.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, salt and sugar and cook for 12 minutes, until pulpy and thick.
Blend to a coarse, jammy paste in a small blender.
Serve warm or at room temperature with flatbread.
notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge in a clean container and freezes well.

recipes.title: Kashmiri Walnut Chutney Doon Chetin
recipes.summary: Walnut and yoghurt chutney with mint and a little chilli, a cooling Kashmiri dip for kebabs and bread.
steps: Blend the walnuts, mint, chilli, garlic and cumin to a coarse paste, until the walnuts are finely chopped.
Stir in the yoghurt, lemon juice and salt.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving so the flavours settle.
notes: Contains tree nuts and dairy. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Kkakdugi Cubed Radish Kimchi
recipes.summary: Crunchy cubes of daikon coated in gochugaru and garlic, the kimchi that goes with soups and rice.

items: 2 tbsp cooked rice, blended with 60ml water

steps: Toss the radish with the salt and sugar and stand for 30 minutes, until it releases liquid.
Drain, keeping 3 tablespoons of the liquid.
Mix the gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger and rice paste, then stir through the radish with the spring onion and the saved liquid.
Pack tightly into a clean jar with the juices covering the radish.
Leave at room temperature for 1 to 2 days until sour and bubbling, then refrigerate.
notes: Salting and fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep the radish under the liquid and burp the jar daily. Discard if there is fuzzy mould or a rotten smell. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.

recipes.title: Oi Sobagi Stuffed Cucumber Kimchi
recipes.summary: Short cucumbers split and stuffed with a spicy chive paste, fresh and snappy within a day.

items: 1 bunch garlic chives, cut in 2cm lengths

steps: Cut each cucumber in 4 lengthways, stopping 2cm from the end, and rub with the salt.
Stand for 20 minutes, then rinse and drain until the surface is no longer slippery.
Mix the carrot, chives, gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, sugar and sesame seeds.
Stuff the paste into the cucumber cuts.
Pack into a clean container and leave at room temperature for 4 hours, then refrigerate.
notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Best eaten within 4 days and kept cold. Discard if slimy or smelling off. Contains fish sauce.

recipes.title: Korean Nabak Kimchi Water Kimchi
recipes.summary: A mild, cool, tangy brined kimchi of cabbage and radish in a lightly salted broth, drunk as well as eaten.
steps: Salt the cabbage and radish for 30 minutes, then drain.
Combine the water, a little extra salt and the sugar in a bowl until dissolved.
Put the vegetables, pear, garlic, ginger, spring onion and chilli in a clean jar.
Pour in the brine to cover.
Leave at room temperature for 1 day, until lightly sour, then refrigerate.
notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keep everything submerged, use clean utensils and discard if cloudy with a rotten smell or mould. Keeps 10 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Japanese Asazuke Quick Cabbage and Cucumber Pickle
recipes.summary: A light salt pickle of cabbage, cucumber and carrot with kombu and yuzu style lemon, ready in an hour.
steps: Rub the salt through the cabbage, cucumber and carrot in a bowl for 1 minute, until it begins to release liquid.
Add the kombu, lemon juice and ginger.
Press under a weighted plate for 15 minutes.
Squeeze out the excess liquid.
Serve cold in small bowls as a side.
notes: Pressing time is not included in prep. Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; discard if it smells off.

recipes.title: Gari Homemade Pickled Sushi Ginger
recipes.summary: Wafer slices of young ginger pickled in sweet rice vinegar, the pink palate cleanser for sushi.
steps: Peel the ginger and slice it paper thin with a mandoline or peeler.
Toss with the salt and stand for 20 minutes, then blanch in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Heat the vinegar and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Pack the ginger and beetroot into a clean jar and pour over the hot vinegar.
Cool, seal and refrigerate for 2 days before using.
notes: Standing and pickling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 months in the fridge in a clean jar with the ginger under the vinegar.

recipes.title: Takuan Style Pickled Daikon
recipes.summary: Sweet and sour yellow daikon pickle, a bright crunchy side for rice bowls.

items: 500g daikon radish, peeled and cut in 5mm rounds

steps: Toss the radish with the salt and stand for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar and turmeric until the sugar dissolves, then cool.
Put the radish and kombu in a clean jar.
Pour in the brine and press the radish under the surface.
Refrigerate for 1 day before serving.
notes: Standing and pickling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge; keep submerged and discard if cloudy or smelling off.

recipes.title: Japanese Goma Dare Sesame Dressing
recipes.summary: Creamy sesame dressing with soy, rice vinegar and mirin for cold noodles, blanched greens and tofu.
steps: Whisk the tahini, vinegar, mirin and soy sauce in a bowl until smooth.
Whisk in the sesame oil, sugar and ginger.
Stir in the water a spoonful at a time, until it pours like thin cream.
Taste and add a little more vinegar if it needs lift.
Serve at room temperature.
notes: Contains sesame and soy. Keeps 1 week in a jar in the fridge; shake before using.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Dua Mon Pickled Mustard Greens
recipes.summary: Sour, lightly fermented mustard greens that sit beside rice, caramelised pork and canh soups.
steps: Wilt the greens in the sun or a low oven for 1 hour, until limp, then pack into a clean jar with the garlic and chilli.
Dissolve the salt and sugar in the water.
Pour over the greens, keeping them under the brine.
Leave in a warm spot for 3 days, tasting daily, until pleasantly sour.
Refrigerate the jar once the greens taste sour.
notes: Wilting and fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep greens submerged, burp the jar daily and discard if there is fuzzy mould or a rotten smell. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.title: Homemade Sauerkraut
recipes.summary: Salted shredded cabbage fermented for a week into tangy, crunchy sauerkraut with caraway.
steps: Rub the salt through the cabbage for 8 minutes, until a lot of liquid comes out.
Mix in the caraway and apple.
Pack firmly into a clean jar, pressing so the liquid covers the cabbage, leaving 4cm of space.
Weigh the cabbage down with a clean small jar or zip bag of brine.
Leave at room temperature for 5 to 7 days, tasting from day 4, then refrigerate.
notes: Fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep the cabbage under the brine at all times, use clean utensils and burp daily. Discard if there is pink or fuzzy mould or a foul smell; a sour, clean smell and cloudy brine are normal. Keeps 3 months in the fridge.

recipes.title: Polish Ogorki Kiszone Sour Pickled Cucumbers
recipes.summary: Small cucumbers fermented in dill and garlic brine, the salty sour pickles of Polish tables.
steps: Dissolve the salt in the water to make a brine.
Pack the cucumbers upright in a clean jar with the dill, garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves and mustard seeds.
Pour in the brine to cover, weighing the cucumbers down.
Leave at room temperature for 4 to 6 days, tasting each day, until sour.
Refrigerate the jar once the cucumbers taste sour.
notes: Fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep submerged, skim any white film, and discard if there is fuzzy mould, slimy cucumbers or a foul smell. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.

recipes.title: Russian Pickled Beetroot with Garlic
recipes.summary: Roasted-style boiled beetroot in a garlic and vinegar marinade, a sharp side for dark bread.
steps: Boil the beetroot for 40 minutes, until a knife slides in, then cool, peel and slice.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, bay leaves and coriander for 3 minutes.
Pack the beetroot and garlic into a clean jar.
Pour over the hot brine to cover.
Cool and refrigerate for 1 day before serving.
notes: Pickling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge with the beetroot under the brine; discard if cloudy or mouldy.

recipes.title: Swedish Pressgurka Pressed Pickled Cucumber
recipes.summary: Thin cucumber slices in sweet vinegar with parsley, served with meatballs and salmon.
steps: Toss the cucumber with the salt and stand for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Stir the vinegar, water and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Mix in the cucumber, parsley and pepper.
Chill for 2 hours so the flavours settle.
Serve cold with meatballs or fish.
notes: Standing and chilling time is not included in prep. Keeps 5 days in the fridge in a covered container.

recipes.title: Danish Rugbrod Seeded Rye Bread
recipes.summary: A dense, sour, seed-packed rye loaf for open sandwiches, with no kneading.
steps: Mix the yeast, honey, yoghurt and water in a bowl.
Add the flours, seeds and salt and stir to a thick, wet dough.
Scrape into a lined loaf tin, smooth and rest for 2 hours, until puffy.
Bake at 200C for 70 minutes, until it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
Cool fully on a wire rack before slicing thinly.
notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keeps 5 days wrapped and freezes in slices.

recipes.title: Lebanese Pickled Turnips with Beetroot Left
recipes.summary: Bright pink pickled root vegetable sticks in a salty brine, the tangy partner to falafel and shawarma.

items: 600g daikon radish, peeled and cut in sticks
1 small raw beetroot, peeled and cut in wedges

steps: Dissolve the salt in the water, then stir in the vinegar.
Pack the radish, beetroot and garlic into a clean jar.
Pour in the brine to cover.
Seal and leave at room temperature for 5 days, until pink and sour.
Refrigerate the jar once the brine turns pink.
notes: Fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep the vegetables submerged and discard if there is fuzzy mould or a foul smell. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.
